title: What if you got struck by lightning? #shorts
description:
300 million volts, air five times hotter than the surface of the Sun... and yet most people survive.

The facts: a lightning bolt carries up to around 300 million volts and heats the air to about 30,000 °C, roughly five times hotter than the Sun's surface (about 5,500 °C). Often much of the current flashes over the skin instead of through the body, which is one reason about 9 in 10 people who are struck survive. Survivors can show Lichtenberg figures: red, fern-like marks on the skin. US park ranger Roy Sullivan was struck seven times and survived every one. If you can hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck.
